Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
On Friday, June 13th at the Annual General Meeting, 
Cllr Tom O’Leary was elected as our 20th Mayor in 
Fingal with Cllr Gráinne Maguire joining him as 
Deputy Mayor. Cllr O’Leary takes over the role 
from former Mayor Cllr Brian McDonagh who was 
elected in June 2024. Over their term, Cllr 
McDonagh and Cllr JK Onwumereh, as Deputy 
Mayor, served with dedication and enthusiasm 
and worked tirelessly on behalf of the people of 
Fingal. I know you will join me in expressing thanks 
to Cllrs McDonagh and Onwumereh for their work 
over the past year within communities across the 
county and their involvement in and support of 
many initiatives. As they begin their terms of office, 
both the Mayor and Deputy Mayor can draw on 
their vast expertise as highly experienced and 
knowledgeable 
public 
servants 
who 
have 
represented their constituents for many years with 
distinction. Also at the AGM, Councillors selected 
the Chairs for the three Fingal’s  Area Committees:  
Balbriggan/Rush-Lusk/Swords, Cllr Luke Corkery. 
Blanchardstown-Mulhuddart/Castleknock/Ongar 
Cllr Eimear Carbone-Mangan.  Howth-Malahide:  
Cllr Cathal Haughey.  On behalf of myself and the 
Management Team, I wish the councillors the very 
best of luck in their respective roles.  
 
I hope you are all enjoying the summer so far. The 
recent spell of good weather has been very 
welcome for the thousands of concert goers who 
flocked to Malahide for this year’s concert series 
which saw 7 international big-name acts perform 
in the stunning surrounds of Malahide Castle & 
Gardens. The concerts began with Charli XCX on 
June 17th followed by Iron Maiden, Neil Young, 
Justin Timberlake, Alanis Morrisette, Duran Duran 
with Nile Rodgers & Chic and finally with Mumford 
& Sons closing off the series on Friday, July 4th. Due 
to the meticulous preparation and effective 
collaboration with all external stakeholders, the 
concert series was another huge success.  
 
Year on year, we are able to attract top performers 
to Malahide in what is the highlight in the concert 
season calendar.  
 
 
 
 
Malahide Castle has proven to be an excellent 
concert venue due to its close proximity to Dublin 
Airport and highly efficient train and bus services 
making it easy for fans to travel to the events. As 
with every large-scale event organised in Fingal, 
the level of planning required is substantial and I 
wish to acknowledge the stellar work carried out 
by the Operations Department, Events Unit, 
Heritage and Conservation Team, Planning and 
Environment Departments in ensuring a fantastic 
time was had by all who attended.  
 
From one fantastic event series to another – the 
always highly anticipated Flavours of Fingal in 
Newbridge House & Farm will take place on the 
weekend of the 5th and 6th of July and we are very 
much looking forward to providing a fantastic 
couple of days for the people of Fingal. Jam packed 
with live musical performances, locally produced 
artisan food and drink, shopping, farming events, 
children’s entertainment and so much more, 
‘Flavours’ is a festival that has grown in stature over 
it's thirteenth years to become one of Ireland’s 
most popular, fun and free summer festivals. The 
expected 70,000 Visitors will be treated to fantastic 
cookery demonstrations in locations around the 
demesne by experts including celebrity chef Kevin 
Dundon, Macken Zawila from The Brooklyn and 
Kelly and Hazel Keogh. Flynn Park, Balbriggan, will 
give thrill seekers of all ages the opportunity to 
have a taste of their activities with trials at archery, 
laser tag, and Crazi-Bugz. The Fingal Village 
marquee is always a popular attraction where our 
departments showcase their work, projects and 
initiatives and offer members of the public 
interactive experiences, advice and information. 
Some of the activities you can look forward to 
include trying out the VR headsets using cutting-
edge Oculus technology at the Digital Services 
stand, 
Fingal 
Arts 
Office 
and 
the 
master 
printmakers from Graphic Studios Dublin who will 
host a hands-on session that brings the magic of 
fine art printing to life and Environment, Climate 
Action, Active Travel & Sports will be collaborating 
to have a Technogym and picker pals activities for 
visitors.

The Fingal Village is a great space to visit to get 
information from the Housing team who will be 
offering information on the Vacant Property 
Refurbishment Grant and the Affordable Housing 
scheme as well as our Economic, Enterprise, 
Tourism & Cultural Development Department who 
will be on hand offering information on European 
Projects. Cognisant of our visitors who needed a 
bit of space away from the excitement of the 
festival, we partnered with Ireland’s Autism 
Charity, AsIAm, to provide The Quiet Zone – this 
space is a calming and welcoming area for those 
with additional needs and, along with a sensory 
map, will ensure an inclusive, enjoyable and safe 
experience for all.  
 
Finally, I am very pleased that construction of the 
€40m centre piece of the Swords Cultural Quarter 
is progressing well and is on schedule to open in 
2027. Culture House Fingal will welcome visitors to 
the library, theatre, gallery, maker space, arts 
spaces and café in a stunning four storey high 
building designed by award-winning architects 
O’Donnell and Twomey and constructed by 
Duggan Brothers. The project represents a key 
capital investment with the majority of the funding 
coming from our own reserves in addition to a 
grant of €3m from the Department of Rural and 
Community Development. Just across the road, 36 
new homes expertly constructed by Duggan 
Brothers, will sit alongside the new building and 
will create a new community on Seatown Road. 
Culture House will be at the heart of Swords and 
will provide visitors with a welcoming and inclusive 
space to immerse themselves in culture, the arts 
and learning. The official launch of Culture House 
Fingal will take place on Culture Night, Friday, 
September 19, and will include the latest updates 
on plans for the new building from the Arts Office 
and Library Service.  
 
Best wishes, 
 
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

Digital Statistics 
The fingal.ie website had 170,052 visitors during 
June which was an increase of 19,726 on the 
previous month. The number of page views rose 
by 25,555 to 363,548 while the average time spent 
on the site rose by seven seconds to 2 minutes and 
1 second. However, the figures for the first six 
months of the year are down on the same period 
in 2024. There have been 876,136 visitors and 
1,911,247 page views since January and visitors 
have spent an average of 1 minute and 59 seconds 
on the site. 
 
The most popular pages during June were Planning 
Applications, Affordable House and the Malahide 
Concerts. A news story on the Council’s decision to 
approve the transformation of Red Island and 
harbour Road in Skerries had over 12,000 page 
views.  
 
The number of followers across the nine corporate 
social media channels rose over the month by 
1,504 to 98,598.  
 
The Facebook account now has 40,892 followers 
and the number of views rose by over 400,000 
during June to 2,452,474 with a reach of 428,122. 
There were 13,978 interactions which was an 
engagement rate of 3.3%. 
 
The most popular post was on June 26 about the 
Iron Maiden Concert at Malalhide Castle with the 
accompanying video having over 114,000 views. 
Instagram now has 14,521 followers and had 
492,896 views during June from a reach f 49,972. 
There were 4,332 interactions which was an 
engagement rate of 9%. The most read post was 
about The Outing Festival in Balbriggan reach of 
3,418 and 104 interactions. 
 
The number of LinkedIn followers is now 11,752. 
There were 62,922 impressions and 990 reactions 
which was an engagement rate of 2%. 
The number of followers on X rose by 13 to 23,398 
and there was an engagement rate of 3.56% from 
160,978 impressions.

The WhatsApp channel now has 3,315 followers 
while the numbers currently following the other 
corporate channels are Threads (1,437), TikTok 
(1,059) and Bluesky (433).

Channel which saw the number of subscribers

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
 
Dublin LA Tourism Network 
The next meeting of the Dublin Local Authority 
Tourism Network is to be hosted by Fingal County 
Council on Thursday 3rd July at Newbridge House. 
The venue will allow the members the chance to 
see the build for Flavours of Fingal in full swing. The 
meeting will discuss items of interest across the 
Dublin region including the marketing of the 
Dublin region, data capture and the upcoming 
IrishFest event in Milwaukee.   
 
Flynn Park Familiarisation Visit 
 
 
 
Page 5 
As part of an early evening familiarisation visit 
organised by Balbriggan Chamber of Commerce, 
the tourism team visited Flynn Park adventure 
centre near Balrothery on 18th June, hosted by 
Shaun Flynn. The visit showcased the major 
attractions of the site including the recently 
installed barrel saunas beside the lake and got to 
hear firsthand about the plans for further 
expansion. Discussions were held on how the 
Council could support and promote the visitor 
attraction.  
 
 
 
 
Fingal Food Circle 
 
 
Preparations are advancing for Fingal Food 
Network’s increased representation at Flavours of 
Fingal 2025. The network will deliver an exciting 
blend 
of 
live 
cooking, 
meet-the-maker 
experiences, and storytelling that brings the 
community’s food heritage to life. Flavours will also 
see the launch of the network's updated brand 
identity ‘Fingal Food Circle’, celebrating the 
evolution of the network and its continued 
collaboration with Fingal County Council and the 
Fingal Farmers Group.

Highlights include the Local Chefs Showcase: 
Daily cooking demos in two locations – the main 
Food Demo Stage and the Artisan Tent in Fingal 
Farmers Field – showcasing local culinary talent in 
action. There will also be a Display Area: Pick up 
your Fingal Food Network Producers’ Bag, meet the 
members behind the produce, and explore the 
newly launched brochure and Fingal food map to 
guide your next local food adventure. The final 
element will be a Meet the Makers Stage: 
Between chef demos, enjoy live interviews with 
producers and growers, sharing stories and 
insights that connect visitors to Fingal’s food 
culture.

Flavours of Fingal County Show 
The Flavours of Fingal County Show is Fingal 
County Council’s flagship annual event, attracting 
up to 70,000 visitors over two days. Held at the 
historic Newbridge House and Farm, this vibrant 
free 
family 
fun 
festival 
seamlessly 
blends 
agriculture, 
Equestrian 
food, 
culture, 
and 
community spirit.

key

the 
show 
features 
everything from local artisan produce and

activities, and interactive exhibitions. Best of all—

At the Flavours of Fingal County Show, Fingal 
County Council proudly showcases its wide range 
of services in the dedicated Fingal Village marquee. 
This interactive space is led by the Communication 
Unit allows members of the public to engage 
directly with staff from across the Council’s 
departments, learn about ongoing initiatives, and 
discover the full scope of services that support 
communities across the county. 
From environment, active travel, sports, arts to 
community 
development, 
tourism, 
libraries, 
emergency services, and more — the Fingal Village 
marquee is a central hub for information, 
engagement, and innovation.

HERITAGE PROPERTIES 
Newbridge House    
Get ready for the return of one of Ireland’s most 
anticipated summer events. The Flavours of Fingal 
County Show 2025 is taking place in the stunning 
parklands of Newbridge House and Farm on the 5th 
& 6th July. 
 
 
Page 7 
Visitors can enjoy not only the vibrant atmosphere 
of the show but also free guided tours of 
Newbridge House and access to the historic 
farmyard, included with admission. It is the perfect 
day out for families, food lovers, and anyone 
looking to experience the best of Fingal’s heritage, 
food, and fun. 
 
Malahide Castle 
“Summer Sessions at the Castle” is coming to the 
breathtaking West Lawn of Malahide Castle & 
Gardens for the first time. This boutique music 
festival promises a magical evening set against the 
stunning backdrop of the castle. 
 
Enjoy a high-energy lineup featuring Ireland’s top 
tribute acts and party bands, along with delicious 
food, a wide range of refreshments, and an 
unbeatable festival atmosphere. 
 
Don’t miss the chance to experience this brand-
new event in one of Dublin’s most iconic outdoor 
venues. 
 
Swords Castle  
 
Markets

The monthly market in Swords Castle continues to 
grow with additional vendors, very good footfall 
and positive reviews. The third Summer food 
market took place in Swords Castle on Saturday, 
21st June.  Plans are in place to expand the spread 
of Summer food markets to other locations in July; 
it is anticipated that similar markets will soon take 
place in both the Malahide Casino and in the 
grounds of St. Patrick’s Church in Donabate.  
 
Ardgillan Castle 
 
 
 
On 24th and 25th July, Ardgillan Castle hosts two 
evening open air theatre productions on the 
terrace performed by the University of South 
Carolina Lancaster Players. On the 24th July, they 
will be performing Beckett’s iconic play ‘Waiting for 
Godot’ and on the 25th July, a new play called ‘On 
the Spectrum’, a touching and thought-provoking 
play that follows the journey of two young adults 
on the autism spectrum as they connect and 
communicate in a world not always built for them.

Page 9

met in June to plan the official programme launch 
in the Lark Concert Hall in September among other 
key upcoming events, including an Arts Office 
funding clinic for local Balbriggan artists and 
community groups in July. At present the support 
team includes members of the Arts Office,

visit to Heart of Glass social arts project in St. 
Helen’s to visit some of its team and view their 
public art murals. Other projects visited included 
Storyhouse in Chester and Art Depot in Finchley, 
Lindon.

of

Awards and residencies 
 
Fingal local writers, Teri Donaghy, Fiona McKay, 
Elaine Maguire O’Connor and Rebecca D’Arcy 
have been chosen for the Irish Writers Centre’s 
prestigious National Mentoring Programme 2025, 
following an exceptional response to this year’s 
nationwide callout, which attracted 354 applicants. 
  
Each selected writer will receive one-to-one 
mentoring from an established writer, offering 
invaluable creative and professional guidance over 
the coming months.   
 
Fingal Arts Office funds the four mentorships to 
guarantee that the chosen awardees receive this 
potentially career-changing support free of charge.

professional artists based in the Fingal area. Each 
awarded artist received a ticket to the Performing 
Arts Forum Limerick Gathering which includes all 
day sessions, lunch, dinner, coffee breaks and the 
artistic programme.  
  
This year four Fingal artists were selected to 
participate, Cliodhna Noonan, Sheila Ryder, 
Tighearnan Noonan and Jacinta Lowndes. 
 
Carnegie 
 
Alannah Thornburgh first Carnegie Musician-
in-Residence  
 
Harper Alannah Thornburg as the inaugural 
Musician-in-Residence at The Carnegie, Swords. 
This exciting new opportunity provides the 
selected musician with an award of €6,000, along 
with space and time to develop their artistic 
practice, create new work and engage with local 
audiences. Drawing on the Samhain concept of a 
time when the boundary between the physical and 
spiritual worlds is at its thinnest, Alannah will 
research local legends and compose new music in 
response. The residency will culminate in a live 
performance of the work in late October to mark 
Samhain.

Cruinniú na nÓg on 7th June, with outdoor dance,

Arts Department continues full steam ahead for 
the Summer months with:

School Tours, July Provision workshop for schools, 
Summer Projects in Film & Music for teens,

available to dispose of their waste i.e. bin sharing 
or bringing their waste to an authorised facility. In 
both instances proof is required in the form of a 
bin sharing agreement whereby 1 household has 
an active bin account in place and an Account No. 
or by providing receipts for disposal of waste if 
bringing waste to a civic amenity centre or waste 
facility.  
 
Initial engagement with householders will be by 
letter communication (July 2025) with a follow up 
reminder letter issued 1 week later. Householders 
will be asked to confirm how they are managing 
their waste by completing a declaration that can be 
filled in online through the Fingal County Council 
website or by return letter. If sufficient proof is 
provided, then those households will be taken off 
the Reverse Register and placed on the Waste 
Register i.e. households who have a waste 
collection service in place.  
 
For Households who don’t engage or respond, 
door to door inspections (Aug/Sept 2025) will be 
carried out to verify on the ground how they are 
managing their waste. It is proposed to target 
4,000 households initially whereby follow up door 
to door inspections may be required for ~ 50% or 
2,000 of those households.  
 
 
 
Page 115 
 
A Fixed Payment Notice (€75 fine) will be issued to 
households who cannot provide proof of how they 
are currently disposing of their waste and a 
direction given under Section 14 of the Waste 
Management Act to put an active bin account in 
place. Legal action through the District Court will 
be taken if households refuse to provide sufficient 
proof that their waste is being managed in 
accordance with the FCC Waste Presentation Bye-
Laws 2020.  
 
 
 
The key objectives of the Waste Presentation Bye-
Laws Project are to: 
1/ Increase participation in household waste 
collection services throughout Fingal. 
2/ Decrease incidents of fly-tipping and illegal 
dumping and associated clean-up costs. 
3/ Increase segregation of waste materials – having 
a 3 bin system in place. 
4/ Reduce the number of waste related complaints 
allowing waste enforcement officers to focus on 
National Waste Priorities.

Strategic Noise Maps  
The Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC, 
which was transposed into Irish law through the 
European Communities (Environmental Noise) 
Regulations 2018 to 2021, requires the local 
authorities within the Dublin agglomeration 
(Dublin City Council, Fingal, Dun Laoghaire 
Rathdown, South Dublin, Wicklow and Kildare 
County Councils) to produce Strategic Noise Maps 
and Noise Action Plans every five years.

The latest Strategic Noise Maps are available on 
the Fingal County Council website at: 
https://www.fingal.ie/environment/noise-
action-plan  
 
The are also available on the EPA website at:  
https://www.epa.ie/our-services/monitoring--
assessment/noise/noise-mapping-and-action-
plans/.  
These maps provide predicted environmental 
noise levels expected from road traffic, rail traffic, 
air traffic and from sites of industrial activity. The 
Strategic Noise Maps are generated using noise 
modelling based on a set of digital datasets, with 
different colours representing different noise 
levels in decibels (dB(A)).   
 
  
 
These maps are required to be updated every 5 
years. The next round of mapping updates is now 
underway, as the new mapping cycle started 
earlier this year. As a designated Noise Mapping 
Body, Fingal County Council inputs into this 
process and liaises with the EPA and other Noise 
Mapping Bodies on all matters related to mapping 
updates.
